full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1-9 (both inclusive) to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 15-3-2006 (decree signed on 22-3-2006) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Manikganj in Title Appeal No. 68 of 2005 allowing the appeal and thereby reversing the judgment and decree dated 28-2-2005 (decree signed on 7-3-2005) passed by the learned Assistant Judge, (in-charge), Daulatpur Court, Manikganj in Title Suit No. 135 of 2000 dismissing the suit, should not be set-aside.

2. The relevant fact giving rise to this Rule, in short, is that one Nekjan Nessa, mother of the plaintiffs purchased the suit property from Shahjahan Mollah by a registered deed on 23-4-1887 and during the survey operation of cadastral Survey, the property was wrongly recorded and published in the name of her husband namely, Riazuddin under Khatian Nos. 127, 255 and 323. After the death of Riazuddin Sheikh his son namely, Manik Mollah instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 403 of 1916 in the concerned court. One Nekjan Nesa was the defendant No. 7 in the said suit and the entire property of Nekjan Nessa made over to her by compromise decree in the said suit. One Asiruddin purchased the suit property from Nekjannesa by a registered deed dated 10-3-1917. During the survey operation of State Acquisition, the record had been recorded and published in equal share in the name of Asir Uddin and his full brother Tasir Uddin under Khatian No. 337. Tasiruddin had no right, title and interest in the portion of the suit property. Asiruddin had been possessing the entire property. The plaintiffs became the owner by succession after the death of Asiruddin. During the survey operation of revisional survey, the name of Asiruddin had been correctly recorded and published and the successors of Asiruddin had been possessing the suit property peacefully. The descendent of Taseruddin sold out the property to defendant Nos. 1-3 by a registered deed dated 3-12-1995. Thereafter, they had been threatening the plaintiffs to dispossess from the suit property and, as such, the plaintiffs instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 2 of 1996 for permanent injunction against the defendant. After receiving the show cause notice of temporary injunction, the defendants erected a Shapra (ছাপড়া) just South West portion of the suit plot and fill up the western portion by cutting earth from the east portion and raised a but on it and, as such, dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit property on 22-1-1996. Hence, the suit for declaration of title and Khan possession of the suit property.

3. The defendant Nos. 1-3 contested the suit by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter-alia, that Asiruddin and Taseruddin were the members of joint family and the two brothers partitioned their property between themselves. Asiruddin executed and registered a deed of relinquishment in favour of Taseruddin on 27-4-1962 and accordingly the SA record was published in the name of two brothers conjointly. Taseruddin died leaving behind two sons and three daughters. After the death of Taseruddin, his heirs instituted a partition suit being No. 169 of 1973. Asiruddin, sons of Taheruddin contested the suit together. Asiruddin made an averment in that suit that he made an oral gift of the half portion of the suit property to Nuru and Hasem. Hasem died leaving behind defendant Nos. 4-11 and the predecessor of defendant sold out 0.40 acre property to defendant Nos.1-3 on 12-12-1995. The defendant Nos. 1-3 purchased the property erected homestead and has been residing thereon. The defendant Nos. 4-8 sold out 0.80 acre on 9-3-1993. Ukil Uddin sold out that property to defendant No.3 on 8-8-1996. The defendant Nos.1-3 have been possessing the property. The plaintiff filed a Title Suit being No. 2 of 1996 praying for permanent injunction which was dismissed. The plaintiffs have not preferred any appeal and the plaintiffs were not dispossessed on 23-1-1996 and the suit of the plaintiff's would be dismissed.

4. The defendant Nos. 25, 26, 28, 40, 46 and 62 supported the plaintiff’s case and stated that the plaintiffs had been dispossessed them since 7 years by erecting but thereon. The defendants did not dispossess the plaintiffs, more so supported them.

5. The defendant Nos. 32-34 made objection against non-impleading of parties in the suit.

6. At the trial, the plaintiffs examined 5 (five) witnesses and the defendants examined 4(four) witnesses and the plaintiffs exhibited their document which were marked as exhibits 1-11. The defendants exhibited their documents which marked as Ka to Umma to prove their respective cases.

7. The learned Judge of the trial court on conclusion of trial, after hearing the parties, considering the evidence and materials on record dismissed the suit by his judgment and decree dated 28-2-2005. Against the said judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred appeal before the learned District Judge, Manikganj. On transfer it was heard and disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Manikganj who after hearing the parties, considering the evidence and materials on record allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court by his judgment and decree dated 15-3-2006.

8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment and decree the defendants as petitioners approached this court and obtained the instant Rule.

9. Mr Md Haroon-ar-Rashid, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioners has placed the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, exhibits, judgment and decree of the courts below and submits that finding of the appellate court as to possession of the plaintiffs before filling title suit No. 2 of 1996 is not in accordance with law which is not sustainable in law. He submits that both the courts below failed to consider that the plaintiff has admitted the oral gift made by Asir Uddin in favour of Nuru and Hasham. He submits that both the courts below failed to discuss as regard to SA Khatian which were recorded in the name of Asir Uddin and Tasiruddin. In support of his contention he has referred the decision reported in: (1) 4 BLC 349.

10. Mr Mohammad Ali Azzam, the learned advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite-parties opposed the rule and submits that the plaintiffs have proved their case by oral and documentary evidence which were entered into evidence as ext. 1-1ka (deeds of ownership), ext. 2, RS and SA Khatian. He submits that the plaintiffs have proved their case as to possession and dispossession. He submits that trial court observed that suit land is esmali property and without partition suit it is not maintainable. In this contention he submits that there is no evidence on record as to esmali property and the appellate court on assessing the evidence correctly reversed the finding of the trial court. He submits that the learned Judge of the trial court observed that the defendant although claimed the suit property by way of oral gift from Asir Uddin but failed to prove by adducing any oral or documentary evidence against which the defendants also failed to any cross-examination as such defendant is not entitle to get any relief. He lastly submits that there is no misreading and non-consideration of evidence passed by the appellate court and the learned Judge of the appellate court considering the evidence and materials on record rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment of the trial court and he prayed for discharged the rule. In support of his contention he has referred the decisions reported in: (1) 14 BLC (AD) 32, (2) 20 BLT (AD) 173 = 14 BLC (AD) 32.

11. In order to appreciate the submissions made by the learned advocates for the parties, I have gone through the revisional application, pleadings, evidence, exhibits and the judgment and decree of the courts below very carefully.

12. Now the question calls for consideration whether the learned Judge of the court of appeal below has committed any error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned judgment and decree.

13. On perusal of the record it appears that the plaintiffs brought a suit for declaration of title and Khas possession. The suit land originally belong to Nekjan Nessa and Nesar Uddin who purchased the suit land by registered deed dated 23-4-1887 which were wrongly recorded in the CS record in the name of her husband Riazuddin. After death of her husband a suit being Title Suit No. 403 of 1916 was filed by her son Manik Molla in the court of 2nd Munsif, Manikgonj where Nekjan Nessa was defendant No.7. The suit was disposed of by amicable Solanama where title of Nekjan Nessa was admitted. Thereafter, Asiruddin purchased the suit land from Nekjan Nessa on 19-3-1917 by registered deed ext. 1ka. It further appears from exts. 3, 3ka SA and RS Khatian 337 that the suit land was recorded in the name of Asir Uddin the present plaintiff opposite-party become the owner and successor of the suit land.

14. On perusal of the judgment of the trial court it appears that the Judge of the trial court dismissed the suit on the ground that the suit land was esmali property without specific schedule or suit for partition, the suit is not maintainable.

15. On perusal of the judgment of the trial court and the appellate court, evidence and other materials on record it appears to me that the suit land originally belong to Nekjan Nessa who sold the suit land to Asir Uddin by a single sale deed dated 19-3-1917 which were duly recorded in his name and after his death the plaintiff opposite-parties become the owner and possessor of the suit land and therefore the question does not arise to make any partition suit.

16. Order VII, rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure clearly stated that where the subject matter of the suit land is immovable property, the plaint shall contain a description of the property sufficient to identify it, and, in case such property can be identified by boundaries or numbers in a record of settlement of survey, the plaint shall specify such boundaries or numbers.

17. In the instant case the suit land is well demarkable by plot numbers RS 705, SA 682 and CS 324 sixteen annas measuring of land 0.52 acres.

<u>18. The claimed of the parties cannot be refused on the mere technical ground when substance is made in the pleadings. Parties’ right to be determined when suit is filed. It is absolutely the domain and discretion of the court to grant the relief sought for or to grant any other general or other relief that may be fit and proper.</u>

<u>19. On perusal of the exhibit lka and evidence on record it appears that the suit land was purchased in the name of Asir Uddin. Therefore it appears to me that the learned Judge of the appellate court considering the evidence and materials on record and assessing the evidence rightly allowed the appeal and set aside the judgment and decree of the trial court.</u>

<u>20. Record of right is evidence of present possession and registered kabala is an evidence of title. The registered document will prevail over the records of rights and would remain in enforce until and unless, such kabala is cancelled by an appropriate civil court. The registered deed dated 19-3-1917 is an old document more than 30 years produced from proper custody presumed under section 90 of the Evidence Act that it was duly executed and genuine documents. This view find supports in the case of:</u>

<u>(1) ADC (Revenue) vs Md Reaz Uddin Pramanik, reported in 5 BLC (AD) 76, wherein their lordships held:</u>

<u>"Once a document more than 30 years old is produced from proper custody under section 90 of the Evidence Act entitles the court to presume that it is a genuine document."</u>

<u>(2) Abdul Mannan Bhuyan vs Md Nasir Hossain, reported in 18 BLC (AD) 44, wherein their lordships held:</u>

<u>"SA and RS records were not an evidence of title and that a registered document would prevail upon the records of rights and that the registered document would remain in enforce unless the same was cancelled by an appropriate civil Court."</u>

<u>(3) Lal Meah vs Haji Md Ibrahim, reported in 28 DLR (AD) 61, wherein their lordships held:</u>

<u>"The record of right raises presumption of possession in favour of person whose name is recorded therein at the time of final publication."</u>

21. On consideration of records it appears to me that findings arrived at by the court of appeal below having been rested upon considerations and discussions of the evidence and the materials on record and also on a correct and proper analysis of the legal aspect involved in the case. Moreover, impugned judgment and decree of the appellate court below in its entirety are well founded in the facts and circumstances of the case and law. Therefore, grounds urged and contentions advanced by the learned advocate for the petitioners are not correct exposition of law. However, I have gone through the decisions cited by the learned advocate for the petitioners reported in 4 BLC 439 are quite distinguishable to that of the instant case and therefore, to that effect I am also unable to accept his submissions. On the contrary the legal pleas taken by the learned advocate for opposite parties prevail and appear to have a good deal of force.

22. In view of the discussions, decisions and reasons stated above, I am of the view that impugned judgment and decree of the court of appeal below suffers from no legal infirmity which calls for no interference by this court in revision. Thus, I find no merit in the Rule.

23. In the result, the Rule is discharged. However, there will be no order as to costs. The judgment and decree dated 15-3-2006 (decree signed on 22-3-2006) passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Manikganj in Title Appeal No. 68 of 2005 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial court are hereby affirmed.

24. The order of stay granted earlier by this Court stands vacated.

Let the Lower Court Records along with a copy of the judgment be sent to the court concerned at once.

End.
